english.title: Begging and wandering abroad
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wandered abroad in a public place, street, highway, court or passage namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) to beg or gather alms
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3 of the Vagrancy Act 1824 and section 70 of the Criminal Justice Act 1982.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
wandered abroad in a
public place/street/highway/court/passage
to beg/gather alms

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence should not be used after 28th June 2026 due to repeal by the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022.
(ii) Made a recordable offence as from 1/12/03 by the National Police Records (Recordable Offences)(Amendment) Regulations 2003.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant wandered abroad in a public place, street, highway, court or passage namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) to beg or gather alms.

welsh.welshoffencetitle: Cardota a chrwydro ar led - Deddf Crwydradaeth 1824
welsh.welshstandardoffencewording: Ar **(..SPECIFY DATE..) yn **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) bu i chi grwydro ar led mewn man cyhoeddus, stryd, priffordd, cwrt neu dramwyfa, sef **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), i gardota neu i gasglucardod
welsh.welshlegislation: Yn groes i Adran 3 Deddf Crwydradaeth 1824 ac Adran 70 Deddf Cyfiawnder Troseddol 1982.

other.powersofarrest: 'Any person' includes a constable. section 26 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 did not abolish this power (confirmed in Gapper v C.C. of Avon and Somerset 1998).
